highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.156.0 improves browser WebGPU packaging, Android texture rendering, and managed graphics and text-shaping performance.
highlights_body: WebGPU browser applications can link against the packaged native archive without compiling its C++ support themselves. Android texture rendering now follows display refresh, while image copying and HarfBuzz text shaping avoid unnecessary managed and native allocations.

bullets.lead: WebGPU support is packaged with browser native assets
bullets.detail: The WebGPU C++ support is now built into libSkiaSharp.a, so browser applications no longer compile it during their final link and C projects avoid incompatible C++ compiler flags.

bullets.lead: Android texture rendering follows the display clock
bullets.detail: Continuous Android GL texture rendering is paced by display refresh rather than buffer-swap throughput, reducing unnecessary paint callbacks while preserving explicit render requests and lifecycle behavior.

bullets.lead: Front-buffered managed streams no longer retain data unnecessarily
bullets.detail: Corrects stream retention so front-buffered managed streams can release data when it is no longer needed.

bullets.lead: Image pixel copies avoid an intermediate allocation
bullets.detail: Managed pixel buffers that can be copied directly now avoid creating an intermediate SKData instance while preserving existing validation behavior.
HarfBuzz UTF-32 buffer input and feature-string formatting reuse managed storage where possible, reducing allocation overhead without changing encoded text or feature decoding.

contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Packaged the WebGPU C++ support inside the browser native archive
contributor_summaries.VirgilMing: Stabilized Blazor CPU sample tests by waiting for the first canvas paint
